events.title: 10-year Treasury yield breaches 5% — global bond selloff
events.why_it_matters: The 10-year briefly hit 5.011% on Sept 14, the highest since 2023, driven by oil, hawkish Fed repricing and heavy supply — a direct valuation headwind for long-duration equities and rate-sensitive sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Whether 5% holds as a ceiling after the FOMC or becomes the new floor, and whether the move spills into credit spreads.

events.title: August CPI — core surprise locks in September hike
events.why_it_matters: Core inflation rose more than expected, pushing Kalshi hike odds from ~61% to 81% in a day and cementing the hawkish repricing across rates and equities.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the oil pass-through keeps core sticky into the Sept 30 PCE print.

events.title: August PCE inflation (Fed's preferred gauge)
events.why_it_matters: July headline PCE was 3.7% y/y and core 3.3% y/y; a hot August print would validate the Fed's hike and keep a second move live into Q4.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m and services ex-housing, the stickiest component.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike delivered; hawkish forecast upgrade
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate to 2.50% (effective Sept 16) with 2027 inflation revised up on Iran-war energy; Lagarde left the door open to more.
events.what_to_watch: EUR rates vs US after Warsh; next ECB is late October.

events.title: China August credit/social financing — bond & equity share tops loans for first time
events.why_it_matters: Social financing stock hit 464.8tn yuan with bond/equity financing exceeding loans for the first time — a structural shift in China's credit engine with implications for banks and growth.
events.what_to_watch: Whether weak loan demand forces another RRR cut or policy-rate reduction.

events.title: US existing home sales fall to 14-month low; mortgage rates up 3rd week
events.why_it_matters: Home sales fell for a third straight month as mortgage rates climbed, confirming the housing market is frozen by the rate shock ahead of the Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the 5% 10-year pushes 30-year mortgage rates above 7.5% and deepens the freeze.

events.title: OPEC+ holds October output quotas unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core-7 kept October targets flat after finishing the 1.65 mbpd rollback, offering no offset to Hormuz/Petroline losses.
events.what_to_watch: Next monthly review is Oct 4 (outside this window); actual output already undershoots quotas because of the war.

events.title: US-China trade truce expires November 10 — pre-summit positioning
events.why_it_matters: The one-year truce deferring punitive tariffs expires Nov 10; the Sept 24 summit is the last realistic window to extend it, so headlines will drive tariff-sensitive names.
events.what_to_watch: Any extension announcement or breakdown in pre-summit talks.

events.title: Government funding — CR signed through Dec 11; shutdown averted
events.why_it_matters: The House passed the Senate's bipartisan CR and the president signed it, funding the government through Dec 11 and removing the Oct 1 shutdown risk entirely past the midterms.
events.what_to_watch: The Dec 11 deadline now becomes the next fiscal flashpoint, after the election.

events.title: Google ad-tech antitrust remedy ruling — no breakup, conduct remedies imposed
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected the DOJ's divestiture demand but ordered interoperability and data-access changes, removing the tail risk of a structural breakup for Alphabet and setting a behavioral-remedy precedent for digital antitrust.
events.what_to_watch: DOJ appeal and whether the conduct remedies meaningfully shift ad-tech share to rivals.

events.title: September PDUFA cluster — 11 FDA decisions (rare disease, oncology, neurology)
events.why_it_matters: September is the busiest PDUFA month of H2 with 11 target action dates, including 8 rare-disease decisions that could be first-ever approvals — binary catalysts for small/mid-cap biotech.
events.what_to_watch: Individual approval/rejection headlines and any FDA safety-signal surprises.

events.title: Oracle FQ1 2027 earnings — beat, cloud infra +121%, backlog $664bn
events.why_it_matters: Adjusted EPS $1.92 vs $1.74 expected and revenue +30% to $19.35bn with a $664bn AI cloud backlog; shares jumped ~7% and lifted the whole AI-infrastructure complex (CoreWeave, Nebius).
events.what_to_watch: Whether the backlog converts to revenue and how the $70bn capex plan is funded.

events.title: Adobe Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: A bellwether for creative-software AI monetization; results landed amid the broader AI-valuation debate.
events.what_to_watch: AI-related ARR disclosure and whether generative AI is cannibalizing or expanding the core.

events.title: Nike FQ1 2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Just outside the window but the key read on global consumer discretionary demand and China recovery; consensus ~$0.44-0.45 EPS, down ~10% y/y.
events.what_to_watch: China revenue trajectory and gross-margin recovery under tariff pressure.

events.title: Accenture FQ4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: IT-services bellwether; consensus ~$3.19 EPS, a read on enterprise AI/tech spending budgets into 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Bookings growth and AI-related consulting demand commentary.

events.title: AI-bubble debate intensifies as S&P 500 sits at record highs
events.why_it_matters: Wall Street is calling it 'crazy days' and 'silly season' with a prominent bear warning of a 'late-stage' AI bubble, while Oracle's $664bn backlog and Nvidia's blowout quarter keep bulls in control — a fragile equilibrium.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Fed hike plus 5% yields trigger a valuation-driven drawdown in AI leaders.

events.title: China rare-earth/strategic-metal export controls; paused restrictions expire Nov 10
events.why_it_matters: China's Order No. 839 licensing regime and the suite of 'paused' export restrictions expiring Nov 10 expose ~$6.5tn of Western downstream production; the Sept 24 summit is the venue to extend the pause.
events.what_to_watch: Any new entity-list additions or signals on the Nov 10 expiry.

events.title: China-Taiwan tensions; Chinese defence forum and mobilization
Trump signs two executive orders on livestock/meat processing competition
events.why_it_matters: Directs USDA to widen State Meat & Poultry Inspection, Cooperative Interstate Shipment and Talmadge-Aiken pathways so ranchers can process and sell meat across state lines, plus antitrust scrutiny of the big four packers — a deregulatory/competition shock to meatpacking margins (Tyson, JBS, Cargill) and a tailwind for small processors.
events.what_to_watch: USDA rulemaking timeline and whether the packer-concentration language converts into an FTC/DOJ action.

events.title: Executive Order 14420/14421 — national emergency over foreign bulk-power system equipment
events.why_it_matters: Invokes IEEPA to create a prohibition-and-licensing framework for foreign-produced grid equipment (utility-scale solar inverters, battery storage, transformers) — a supply-chain and cost shock for renewables/utilities and a tailwind for domestic manufacturers; published in the Federal Register Aug 31, inside the window's run-up.
events.what_to_watch: Commerce/DOE implementing rules and which countries/components land on the prohibited list.

events.title: Senate procedural vote on CLARITY Act crypto market-structure bill
events.why_it_matters: Senate Republicans released a new version of the CLARITY Act on Sept 14 and the chamber votes Tuesday on advancing it; prediction-market odds surged and Bitcoin rallied — the single biggest US crypto-regulatory catalyst of the quarter, with direct read-through to COIN, exchanges, stablecoin issuers and miners.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the motion to proceed clears 60 votes and which amendments (ethics, SEC/CFTC split) get attached.

events.title: OFAC designations — transnational criminal organizations and counter-terrorism; VTB Bank sanctioned for Iran evasion
events.why_it_matters: OFAC designated TCO/counter-terrorism targets on Sept 9 and the State Department sanctioned Russia's VTB Bank on Sept 14 for aiding Iran's sanctions evasion — widening the financial perimeter around the Iran war and raising secondary-sanctions risk for banks and shippers.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-on designations of Iranian oil buyers and any Treasury action on shadow-fleet tankers.

events.title: Commerce export controls targeting Chinese access to remote AI servers (AI diffusion rule successor)
events.why_it_matters: The administration's cut-down AI diffusion rule, reportedly targeting Chinese access to remote AI compute, could be shared with industry as soon as September — a direct overhang on Nvidia/AMD China revenue and on cloud providers leasing compute to Chinese-linked entities.
events.what_to_watch: BIS publication of the interim final rule and whether it captures third-country (Malaysia, Singapore) transshipment.

events.title: EU prepares 'Buy European' public-procurement rules aimed at China
events.why_it_matters: Brussels is expected to unveil procurement rules favouring European firms in public contracts, and EU/China trade chiefs hold a crunch videoconference Thursday — a fresh EU-China trade friction thread the primary did not carry.
events.what_to_watch: Publication date of the procurement regulation and whether Beijing retaliates against EU exporters.

events.title: University of Michigan September preliminary sentiment — 47.8, 1-yr inflation expectations jump to 4.6%
events.why_it_matters: Sentiment fell 3.9 points to 47.8 (down 7.5% m/m) while year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.6%, the highest since June — the stagflation signal that sits directly behind the Fed's hike and is a core input to the SEP.
events.what_to_watch: The final September print (Sept 26) and whether 5-10yr expectations also drift higher.

events.title: Initial jobless claims — 206k (week of Sept 10), matching expectations
events.why_it_matters: Claims held at a low 206k, down 1k, keeping the labour market tight enough to validate the Fed's hike and undercut the 'Fed is hiking into a weakening economy' argument.
events.what_to_watch: Next print Sept 17 and whether the insured-unemployment rate starts to drift up.

events.title: 30-year Treasury auction — $22bn stops at 5.308%, bid-to-cover 2.61x
events.why_it_matters: Strong demand (2.61x vs 2.4x 12-month average, stopped 2.7bp through when-issued) at a 5.308% high yield — the key test of whether the 5% 10-year regime is a supply problem or a term-premium repricing, and it passed.
events.what_to_watch: The 10-year and 20-year auctions later in September and whether foreign/indirect bid share holds.

events.title: EIA weekly petroleum and natural gas storage — crude -0.4mb, gas +40 Bcf to 3,254 Bcf
events.why_it_matters: Refinery utilisation ran at 97.8% with crude stocks drawing modestly, while gas storage sits 79 Bcf below last year — the physical backdrop to the Brent spike and a live input for winter gas/power pricing.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Iran-war supply disruption starts showing up as a US crude build or a product-crack blowout.

events.title: Copper hits record $14,875/t on LME then crashes 4.7% on stalled US tariff decision
events.why_it_matters: A record intraday high followed by a 4.7% COMEX collapse on a stalled Section 232 copper tariff decision shows the metals complex is now trading policy risk rather than physical fundamentals — a warning for the whole tariff-sensitive commodity complex.
events.what_to_watch: The timing of the copper tariff determination and whether the record-to-crash pattern repeats in aluminium or steel.

events.title: Lennar FQ3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: EPS est. $1.30 on $8.37bn revenue, landing the same day as the Fed decision and one week after existing home sales hit a 14-month low — the cleanest read on whether 5%+ mortgage rates have broken the new-home order book and on builder incentive/margin compression.
events.what_to_watch: New orders, cancellation rate and gross margin guidance versus the June quarter's -4% order decline.

events.title: General Mills and the Sept 13-20 second-tier earnings cluster (26 companies)
events.why_it_matters: General Mills leads the packaged-food read on input costs and price elasticity at a moment when oil-driven freight and grain costs are rising and the consumer is deteriorating — a sector bellwether the primary skipped entirely.
events.what_to_watch: Organic sales growth and any gross-margin guidance cut tied to freight/energy.

events.title: UK and Japan August inflation prints land alongside BoE/BoJ decisions
events.why_it_matters: UK CPI (~3.7% prior) and Japanese CPI publish in the same 48 hours as the BoE hold and the BoJ hike, so a hot UK print could flip the BoE to a hike and a hot Japan print would harden the yen-carry unwind case.
events.what_to_watch: UK services CPI and Japan core-core; any BoJ language on the pace beyond 1.25%.

events.title: UK August CPI (pre-BoE)
events.why_it_matters: Last inflation print before the Sept 17 MPC; energy from the Iran war has revived hike talk even though a hold is the base case.
events.what_to_watch: Whether headline/core re-accelerate enough to flip the expected 6-3 hold toward a hike or a more hawkish statement.

events.title: August housing starts and building permits
events.why_it_matters: With existing sales at a 14-month-style low and the 10-year at 5%, another weak starts/permits print would confirm the rate shock is hitting new construction, not just resale.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts vs permits; a permits collapse is the leading signal for homebuilder multiples.

events.title: US industrial production and capacity utilization (August)
events.why_it_matters: First hard activity print after the oil shock and into the Fed hike; factory output vs mining/utilities will show whether energy disruption is already hitting production.
events.what_to_watch: Manufacturing IP and capacity utilization; a drop would feed the growth-scare side of stagflation.

events.title: PBoC September LPR fixing
events.why_it_matters: 1y LPR has been 3.00% and 5y 3.50% for 15 months; a hold after weak retail/FAI/credit would confirm Beijing is not delivering a rate bazooka.
events.what_to_watch: Any 5y LPR cut (mortgages) vs another hold plus liquidity ops only.

events.title: August JOLTS job openings
events.why_it_matters: Last major labor print in the window after the FOMC; still-tight openings would keep a second 2026 hike live, a slide would argue the Sep hike is a one-and-done.
events.what_to_watch: Openings/unemployed ratio and quits; a break lower would be the first real labor-cooling signal Warsh would have to address.

events.title: Bank of Korea minutes show rift after hike to 3.00%
events.why_it_matters: Minutes of the Aug 27 25bp hike to 3.00% show a possible split on back-to-back tightening, a signal for KRW and Korean duration as BoJ/Fed also hike.
events.what_to_watch: Language on the next move and any hint that chip/export strength is being outweighed by household-debt stress.

events.title: August CPI — core 0.3% MoM locks in September hike
events.why_it_matters: Headline +0.4% MoM / 3.4% y/y; core +0.3% MoM (hot vs ~0.2%) even as core y/y eased to 2.4%; hike odds jumped into the 80s.
events.what_to_watch: How much of the heat was energy/oil pass-through versus stickier core services heading into Warsh's SEP.

events.title: August PPI — energy/diesel spike
events.why_it_matters: Final-demand PPI +0.4% MoM / +5.4% y/y with goods +1.1% and diesel +24.1% shows the Hormuz shock already in the pipeline before CPI and the Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Pass-through into September CPI goods and any Fed language on energy as 'transitory'.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike; hawkish forecast upgrade
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate to 2.50% (effective Sept 16) with 2027-28 inflation and 2026-27 growth revised up, explicitly citing Middle East energy inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether euro-area duration keeps cheapening as the new rates take effect tomorrow and oil stays >$100.

events.title: China August credit — loans and TSF miss badly
events.why_it_matters: New yuan loans were only +60bn yuan vs ~400bn expected (after July's -340bn); TSF stock growth slowed to 7.2% and household loans stayed negative.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Sept 20 LPR or extra fiscal support follows; banks remain the transmission bottleneck.

events.title: US existing-home sales at 14-month-class low
events.why_it_matters: Sales fell 2% to 3.98mn SAAR as 30-year rates rose to 6.67%; inventory at 4.9 months is the highest since 2015, confirming a frozen housing market into the hike.
events.what_to_watch: Lennar (Sept 16) and Thursday starts for confirmation that the freeze is spreading to builders.

events.title: Trump Ukraine-Russia energy-infrastructure truce proposal
events.why_it_matters: Kremlin called an energy-strike halt 'very good' but tied it to sanctions relief; Kyiv wants reciprocity. Russian diesel export bans already tighten global distillate.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a verified moratorium starts and if Moscow's sanctions-lift demand kills it; diesel cracks vs crude.

events.title: FY2027 CR signed — shutdown averted through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 6500 funds agencies at FY2026 levels through Dec 11, removing the Oct 1 shutdown tail before midterms; debt-limit X-date is 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing in this window; next cliff is Dec 11 post-election.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies: no AdX breakup
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ's forced sale of Google's ad exchange and imposed behavioral remedies, the second major Google case to spare structural breakup.
events.what_to_watch: Unsealed remedy text and DOJ appeal risk; Apple-Epic SCOTUS argument is October-term, outside this window.

events.title: Lennar Q3 earnings (housing bellwether)
events.why_it_matters: Consensus EPS ~$1.29-1.32 and revenue ~$8.4bn, both down y/y, landing the same day as the FOMC with mortgage rates following the 5% 10-year.
events.what_to_watch: Orders, cancellations, incentives, and FY guide; a cut would confirm the housing freeze is in earnings, not just NAR prints.

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (HNUC) pricing window
events.why_it_matters: Largest US IPO in the window (~$750-900mn, ~$8.5-10.2bn valuation) is a pure AI-power/nuclear tape test after the roadshow launched Sept 8.
events.what_to_watch: Final price vs $15-18 range and first-day demand as a read-through for SMRs and Palisades.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) day-105 lockup tranche
events.why_it_matters: Staggered post-June 12 IPO unlocks continue (~7% tranche around day 105) after a large Sept 9-10 release, a supply overhang into year-end.
events.what_to_watch: Actual vs theoretical float and whether the Oct earnings-triggered tranche is telegraphed.

events.title: SEMICON India 2026
events.why_it_matters: Modi-inaugurated show with 600+ exhibitors is the post-SEMICON Taiwan venue for capex, China+1, and subsidy headlines in a still-hot AI-chip cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Any TSMC/Intel/Samsung/India incentive announcements that re-route 2027 fab dollars.

events.title: Atlantic hurricane season still record-quiet
events.why_it_matters: No hurricanes yet in the satellite era's latest start; El Niño shear has spared Gulf oil/LNG just as Hormuz is impaired — a one-sided energy shock.
events.what_to_watch: The Bermuda trough (~40% development odds) — only a western-Gulf track would add a second supply shock.

events.title: House tees up H.R. 5334 Graham Russia/Iran sanctions (secondary tariffs)
events.why_it_matters: Senate-passed bill authorizes up to 500% tariffs on Russian goods and up to 100% on top buyers of Russian oil/gas (China, India, Turkey, etc.) plus an Iran Sanctions Act extension through 2031 — a live secondary-tariff shock on top of Hormuz.
events.what_to_watch: House rule debate today and expected floor vote Sept 16 before recess; whether Democrats strip or narrow the presidential tariff authority.

events.title: EPA finalizes repeal of 2024 power-plant GHG standards
events.why_it_matters: Largest U.S. power-sector deregulatory action in years: EPA struck most of the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards (CCS-or-retire) and proposed wiping remaining GHG standards, claiming ~$310bn in savings and a large lift to coal-for-power.
events.what_to_watch: Federal Register effective date, litigation from states/NGOs, and whether the companion proposal to kill remaining CAA 111 GHG authority is finalized.

events.title: OFAC Operation Economic Outcast: 36 Iran aviation designations
events.why_it_matters: Distinct from the later VTB/TCO hits: Treasury sanctioned 27 remaining Iranian airlines plus third-country facilitators and suspended Iran aviation general licenses, expanding secondary-sanctions risk for global aviation, cargo, and banks.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-on designations of GSAs/lessors, airline overflight/parts disruption, and any EU/UK alignment.

events.title: EO 14427 — DPA energy delegations split Interior/Energy
events.why_it_matters: Amends EO 13603 so Interior and Energy independently exercise Defense Production Act authorities over energy production, construction, and related materials, with Energy Dominance Council dispute resolution — a priority-order tool for fuels, minerals, and grid kit.
events.what_to_watch: First DPA priority ratings or allocation orders under the dual-secretary setup.

events.title: FCC publishes Consolidated Prohibited Entities List
events.why_it_matters: Operationalizes equipment-authorization bans by merging Covered List, BIS Entity/MEU, UFLPA, NS-CMIC and NDAA lists — a compliance shock for radio/network gear importers and a tailwind for non-China vendors.
events.what_to_watch: Which OEMs lose FCC IDs and any downstream shortages in radios, modules, and network kit.

events.title: FDA approves Isembyld (apitegromab) for SMA muscle loss
events.why_it_matters: First FDA-approved myostatin-pathway add-on for SMA (Scholar Rock) — a binary already inside the September PDUFA cluster the primary only flagged as upcoming Sept 16–30.
events.what_to_watch: Launch uptake vs nusinersen/risdiplam background therapy and any other landed September PDUFAs.

events.title: NDRC offers 36 projects (¥61.4bn) to private capital
events.why_it_matters: Beijing's response to collapsing private FAI: transport, logistics, water, wind/storage/charging projects aiming to pull ¥15.6bn of private money — a policy signal, not a demand impulse yet.
events.what_to_watch: Whether private firms actually bid and if a standing project-recommendation pipeline follows.

events.title: $39bn 10-year note reopening stops through at 4.834%
events.why_it_matters: Primary logged the weak-ish 30-year but missed the 10-year: BTC 2.71x and 79.2% indirects showed real demand even as yields sat near multi-year highs — a key read on who is absorbing duration before the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether that bid survives if the 10-year holds above 5% after the Sept 16 hike.

events.title: Euro area ZEW sentiment slumps to 25.8; inflation expectations jump
events.why_it_matters: First post-ECB-hike investor survey: euro-area ZEW dropped to 25.8 from 31.4 (miss vs ~40) while inflation expectations surged — hawkish-growth mix that validates the ECB's energy-inflation upgrade.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through into Sept 23 eurozone flash PMIs and Bunds vs the Fed/BoE/BoJ cluster.

events.title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey (September)
events.why_it_matters: First regional factory print into FOMC day-minus-one after August's four-year high (20.6); consensus ~14 still expansion but a miss would feed the 'rates too high for housing/goods' tape.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 14-ish consensus, plus prices-paid and new orders into Thursday's Philly Fed.

events.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (September)
events.why_it_matters: August's 47.4 was the hottest since 2021; a second strong print the morning after FOMC would complicate the 'demand is cracking' narrative, a collapse would do the opposite.
events.what_to_watch: General activity, prices paid, and employment vs the still-hot August base.

events.title: EIA weekly crude/products (week ending Sept 11)
events.why_it_matters: With Hormuz impaired and Brent ~$107, the next inventory print (and any SPR draw) is a higher-beta oil event than a normal Wednesday EIA; primary only covered the Sept 4 week.
events.what_to_watch: Crude vs gasoline/distillate builds, SPR change, and implied demand given diesel already in PPI.

events.title: Eurozone flash PMIs (September)
events.why_it_matters: First activity read after the hawkish ECB hike and today's weak ZEW; August composite 52.1 was still expanding on German defense/AI demand.
events.what_to_watch: Germany manufacturing vs services, employment, and input prices given energy-war inflation.

events.title: UK August CPI (ahead of BoE)
events.why_it_matters: ONS prints at 07:00 UK time; July was 2.9% y/y and consensus is ~3.1% as energy from the Iran war feeds through.
events.what_to_watch: A hot print would lift the minority-hike camp on the MPC the next day; a cool print cements a hold.

events.title: August industrial production and capacity utilization
events.why_it_matters: Factory output is the real-side check on whether oil/tariff cost-push is already cutting activity as the Fed hikes.
events.what_to_watch: Manufacturing vs mining/utilities split; a drop would reinforce stagflation, a beat would validate a hawkish Fed.

events.title: August CPI — core monthly surprise locked in September hike
events.why_it_matters: Headline 3.4% y/y and a hotter-than-forecast 0.3% core MoM pushed hike odds into the high-80s/90s and cemented the hawkish repricing.
events.what_to_watch: How Warsh treats sticky services vs energy in tomorrow's statement; the print itself is done.

events.title: August PPI — energy-led wholesale inflation
events.why_it_matters: Final-demand PPI +0.4% MoM / +5.4% y/y with goods +1.1% and diesel +24.1% confirmed oil is already in the pipeline to CPI.
events.what_to_watch: Pass-through into September CPI/PCE; no further PPI until Oct 15.

events.title: China August credit — loans miss; bonds/equity exceed loans YTD
events.why_it_matters: New yuan loans only +60bn vs ~400bn expected; AFRE stock 464.8tn, with bond+equity >50% of YTD incremental financing for the first time.
events.what_to_watch: Bank NIMs vs capital-market financing; weak loan demand argues for more easing that has not arrived.

events.title: US existing-home sales fall to 2026 low
events.why_it_matters: August sales 3.98mn SAAR (-2.0% MoM); months' supply 4.9, highest since 2015, as 30-year mortgages sit ~6.5-6.8%.
events.what_to_watch: Lennar print and Sept 17 housing starts for confirmation the freeze is spreading to new construction.

events.title: Saudi East-West pipeline (Petroline) shut after drone attacks
events.why_it_matters: The main Hormuz bypass (design up to 7 mbpd) went offline Sept 11 after drones hit pumping stations; Yanbu stocks are only days of cover and repairs may take 3-8 weeks.
events.what_to_watch: Partial restart headlines vs further Red Sea/Houthi disruption; this is why Brent is still >$105.

events.title: UNGA High-level Week / Trump General Debate speech
events.why_it_matters: High-level week 18-28 Sep (General Debate 22-26 and 28); Trump's UNGA remarks are a live oil/Iran/China headline risk two days before Xi arrives.
events.what_to_watch: Ceasefire/Hormuz language vs doubling-down; any unscripted tariff or Taiwan comments.

events.title: Canada retaliatory tariffs on ~C$27.6bn of US goods
events.why_it_matters: 15/25/50% counter-tariffs on steel, dairy, appliances, furniture, apparel and ag equipment took effect Sept 8, triggering the US Sept 8 proclamations.
events.what_to_watch: Pass-through into US exporter earnings (industrials/consumer) and whether talks reopen around the UNGA window.

events.title: FY2027 CR signed — shutdown risk deferred to Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: House 370-48 CR (P.L. 119-103) funds government through Dec 11 at FY2026 levels, removing a Sept 30 shutdown from this window.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing until after midterms; December fight is the next real risk. Quiet this fortnight.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies: no breakup, behavioral only
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ's AdX divestiture; Google keeps the stack. Full opinion due unsealed ~Sept 16; parties have ~30 days for a final judgment.
events.what_to_watch: Unsealed opinion Sept 16 and any DOJ appeal; pattern of behavioral-not-structural Google remedies continues.

events.title: FedEx Q1 FY2027 earnings (freight/oil-cost bellwether)
events.why_it_matters: Global parcel/freight read-through on volumes, fuel surcharges and China/US demand as Brent holds >$105; Street EPS ~$4.04-4.21, sales ~$22.6bn.
events.what_to_watch: Fuel-cost guidance, Asia volumes, and any demand warning that would confirm a growth slowdown under higher rates.

events.title: Mega-cap earnings this week — quiet
events.why_it_matters: No Mag-7/mega-cap reports this week (~0% of S&P earnings weight); index will be driven by the Fed, oil and rates, not stock-specific prints.
events.what_to_watch: Next week AutoZone (Sept 22); Nike/Accenture are Oct 1 (outside window).

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (HNUC) pricing/listing
events.why_it_matters: Largest nuclear-equipment IPO of the window: 50m shares at $15-18 (~$750-900m) into AI/data-center power demand; dual-class leaves public ~1% of votes.
events.what_to_watch: Deal size vs range, first-day trading, and whether nuclear/SMR sentiment holds with 5% yields.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) staggered lockup — next ~328m-share tranche
events.why_it_matters: Day-105 unlock of ~328m shares after the Sept 9-10 ~378m-share releases already hit the tape; rolling supply is a known volatility source in a ~$2tn name.
events.what_to_watch: Actual insider selling vs eligibility; Oct 9/24 tranches follow. Sept 9 tranche already resolved.

events.title: South Korea semiconductor export boom vs BOK hikes
events.why_it_matters: August SK exports +68.7% y/y on AI memory; BOK already at 3.00% after back-to-back hikes (minutes today showed a 6-1 split). TSMC is lifting 3nm output ~70% over 18 months.
events.what_to_watch: Whether global rate shock/oil hits AI capex, or the supercycle offsets Fed/BoJ tightening for chip equities.

events.title: IG Metall Germany auto protests (job-cut wave)
events.why_it_matters: Union targeting 100k+ participants at 200+ sites (VW, Mercedes, Porsche, Bosch, suppliers) against EV/China-driven job cuts — Europe auto employment already at a 20-year low.
events.what_to_watch: Whether protests escalate into warning strikes that hit production, vs one-day political theatre.

events.title: US East/Gulf ILA dockworkers — strike averted
events.why_it_matters: ILA approved a 6-year deal (wages $39→$63, automation protections), removing a coastwide port-strike tail risk from this window.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation/local ratification noise only; European port warning strikes (Rotterdam Sept 4, German ports early Sept) already faded.

events.title: Commerce final AD/CVD on solar cells from India, Indonesia, Laos
events.why_it_matters: Final dumping/subsidy margins are steep (India ~123% AD + 126% CVD; Indonesia AD 94% and CVD 73–174%; Laos AD 65% and CVD 82–154%), a supply-cost shock for US solar developers and a tailwind for domestic module makers if ITC affirms injury.
events.what_to_watch: USITC final injury vote on 2026-10-14; if affirmative, Commerce issues orders around 2026-11-02 and cash deposits lock in.

events.title: European Parliament adopts CBAM expansion / anti-circumvention mandate
events.why_it_matters: MEPs voted 464–50–159 to push CBAM from basic materials into hundreds of downstream steel/aluminium goods and to tighten China-linked resource-shuffling rules, raising carbon-cost risk for exporters into the EU.
events.what_to_watch: Trilogue vs Council's narrower ~200-product list and whether a 2028 start for downstream extension survives; related Temporary Decarbonisation Fund also advanced.

events.title: MIIT/NDRC 15th Five-Year Plan for electronic information manufacturing
events.why_it_matters: Official plan targets scale-above electronics revenue above 30 trillion yuan by 2030, 3.5% R&D intensity, and full-chain IC/AI-hardware/advanced-computing catch-up — a state-capacity signal into semis, servers, and energy electronics.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through funding, equipment localization, and whether the plan hardens export-control retaliation risk around the Sept 24 Trump-Xi window.

events.title: China State Council notice on SME overdue-payment governance
events.why_it_matters: Beijing is forcing large firms/SOEs toward cash payment within 60 days and capping commercial bills, a cash-flow transfer from big buyers to SMEs after industrial receivables hit ~28.9tn yuan.
events.what_to_watch: SOE accounts-payable rundowns, commercial-bill issuance, and whether the squeeze hits listed SOE working capital into Q4.

events.title: FDA opens Expedited IND pilot under Operation TrialBlazer
events.why_it_matters: FDA began taking paired sponsor/QRI applications for a pilot meant to shorten time-to-first-in-human studies, a deregulatory catalyst for early-stage biotech versus China/Australia trial venues.
events.what_to_watch: Application cutoff 2026-10-30 and which 8–10 pairs FDA selects; this is process reform, not a PDUFA binary.

events.title: Japan Q2 GDP revised up to 1.4% annualized
events.why_it_matters: Second print lifted real GDP to +0.4% q/q / +1.4% annualized on a narrower capex drop, keeping a third straight expansion in place ahead of this week's BoJ hike decision — but consumption is still basically flat.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the revision hardens the 1.25% hike call on 2026-09-17/18 or is dismissed as war-quarter noise.

events.title: Treasury doubles long-end coupon buybacks; $6bn 10–20yr op
events.why_it_matters: Liquidity buybacks in 10–30yr paper were lifted from $2bn to at least $4bn (first op sized at $6bn) just as the 10-year was breaking 5% — a duration-supply offset, not QE, and it did not stop the selloff.
events.what_to_watch: Subsequent long-end ops through the Nov 4 refunding and whether dealers keep offering 8–18x the cap.

events.title: AutoZone Q4 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: High-multiple off-price auto-parts bellwether is a clean read on US DIY/DIFM demand and ticket inflation after the rate shock; it sits outside the primary's Sept 13–20 cluster.
events.what_to_watch: SSS, gross margin vs oil/freight costs, and FY2027 guidance vs ~$54.3 EPS / ~$6.7bn sales consensus.

events.title: US August housing starts and building permits
events.why_it_matters: Confirms whether the rate shock that already cut existing-home sales to a 2026 low is also freezing new construction.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family starts versus permits; a sharp drop would hit homebuilders (Lennar reports the same week) and building-product names.

events.title: China September LPR fixing
events.why_it_matters: 1y LPR 3.0% and 5y 3.5% have been on hold 14+ months; after weak August credit/activity, a hold would confirm Beijing is still prioritizing the yuan and exports over demand support.
events.what_to_watch: Any 10-25bp cut versus another hold; Polymarket-style odds still heavily favor no change by month-end.

events.title: UMich consumer sentiment final (September)
events.why_it_matters: Prelim crashed to 47.8 on Sept 11 (vs ~51 expected) with 1-year inflation expectations jumping to 4.6% on fuel and trade fears.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the final revises expectations/inflation views after the FOMC and another week of $100+ oil.

events.title: August JOLTS
events.why_it_matters: First labor-market print after the FOMC; August NFP already beat at +162k with unemployment 4.1%.
events.what_to_watch: Openings and quits as a read on whether the hike is landing on a still-tight labor market.

events.title: Lennar Q3 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Bellwether homebuilder reports after the close as existing-home sales hit a 2026 low and mortgage rates sit in the mid/high-6s heading toward 7%.
events.what_to_watch: Orders, incentives, cancellation rate, and 2026/27 guidance versus ~$1.29 EPS / ~$8.37bn sales consensus.

events.title: FedEx Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global freight/volume read-through on trade, oil-driven costs, and US-China/Canada tariff friction; consensus ~$22.6bn sales / ~$4.04-4.21 EPS.
events.what_to_watch: Express vs ground volumes, fuel surcharge commentary, and any China/Asia trade warning.

events.title: Costco Q4 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Largest consumer print in a quiet mega-cap earnings window; lands the same day as the Trump-Xi summit.
events.what_to_watch: Traffic, mix, gasoline, and any tariff/food-inflation commentary versus ~$6.36-6.55 EPS consensus.

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (HNUC)
events.why_it_matters: Largest pure-play nuclear listing of the window (~50m shares, $15-18, ~$825m at midpoint, ~$9bn valuation) aimed at SMR-300 and Palisades restart as data-center power demand collides with $100+ oil.
events.what_to_watch: Whether it prices/trades given 5% 10-year yields and dual-class voting (~1% for public Class A).

events.title: FDA Expedited IND Pilot (Operation TrialBlazer)
events.why_it_matters: Application window opens to shorten US first-in-human timelines versus China/Australia; niche but constructive for biotech development speed.
events.what_to_watch: Which 8-10 sponsor-QRI pairs are selected (notifications around Dec 18); window closes Oct 30.

events.title: August PPI — energy-led 0.4% MoM / 5.4% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation re-accelerated with final-demand goods +1.1% and diesel +24.1% MoM, confirming the oil shock is entering producer prices ahead of the Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Pass-through into September CPI/PCE if Hormuz/pipeline outages persist.

events.title: August NFP +162k, unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: Jobs beat (~56k expected) with upward revisions gave the Fed cover to hike even as housing and sentiment cracked.
events.what_to_watch: Already in the rear-view for this FOMC; next labor color is JOLTS on Sept 29.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike and hawkish forecast upgrade
events.why_it_matters: Second 2026 hike; 2027-28 inflation and 2026-27 growth forecasts raised, with Iran-war energy cited; deposit-rate move effective Sept 16.
events.what_to_watch: EUR rates/banks versus duration and rate-sensitive EU cyclicals as energy inflation peaks toward 3.6% in Q4.

events.title: China August credit/TSF miss; bond/equity share tops loans
events.why_it_matters: New TSF CNY 1.66tn vs ~2.0-2.15tn expected; new loans only CNY 60bn vs ~420bn; outstanding loan growth a record-low 4.9% while stock TSF hit 464.8tn yuan.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the bond/equity > loans mix is a healthy marketization shift or just loan demand collapse.

events.title: OPEC+ holds October quotas unchanged
events.why_it_matters: The core seven kept October quotas flat after finishing the 1.65mbpd unwind, offering no offset to Hormuz losses; next review is Oct 4.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance vs war-impaired actual output, and any emergency meeting if Brent spikes further.

events.title: CR funds government through Dec 11 — shutdown risk cleared
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 6500 / PL 119-103 removes the Oct 1 shutdown cliff through the midterms; debt limit is a 2027 problem ($41.1tn cap).
events.what_to_watch: Nothing in this window; next cliff is Dec 11 lame-duck.

events.title: South Korea semiconductor export boom (Aug / early Sept)
events.why_it_matters: August chip exports ~$46.7bn (+~209% y/y); Sept 1-10 chips ~$16.5bn (+270%) as AI memory/SSD demand offsets the oil/rates shock for semis.
events.what_to_watch: Whether hyperscaler capex commentary into Q4 stays intact if the Fed/BoJ tighten into a 5% 10-year.

events.title: SEC proposes full rescission of adviser pay-to-play Rule 206(4)-5
events.why_it_matters: A 3-2 Atkins majority moved to scrap the 2010 ban on compensated government-client work after covered political contributions, a live midterm-year compliance and First Amendment fight for asset managers and placement agents.
events.what_to_watch: Comments close Nov 9; the rule stays in force until a final vote, and MSRB G-37/FINRA 2030 would still constrain municipal/pay-to-play conduct.

events.title: Ways and Means markup of Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act (H.R. 10357)
events.why_it_matters: Separate from the Senate CLARITY market-structure vote, the 114-page tax draft would add a $10 de minimis fee exemption, extend wash-sale/constructive-sale rules to crypto, and lock ordinary-income treatment for mining/staking.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the committee reports the bill before the pre-election recess; wash-sale language is the price-moving piece for traders even if floor action slips.

events.title: ECJ C-319/24 P — Commission v Sinopec on China PVA anti-dumping
events.why_it_matters: The Court of Justice reviewed how Brussels may construct 'normal value' and use facts-available for non-cooperating Sinopec entities in a China-distortion anti-dumping case, a template for other chemical/industrial AD duties.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the judgment restores Commission discretion on Article 2(6a)/2(10) calculations and spills into pending EU duties on Chinese chemicals, EVs, and batteries.

events.title: China eight-ministry smart-home consumption action plan
events.why_it_matters: MOFCOM/NDRC/MIIT and five other agencies tied smart-home subsidies, interoperability standards, and elderly-care hardware to the 2026 trade-in program (¥250bn ultra-long special bonds), a demand kicker for appliances, sensors, and home robots.
events.what_to_watch: Provincial subsidy catalogs and whether trade-in money actually rotates into whole-home upgrades versus food/auto categories.

events.title: EU sets early-October deadline for Chinese action on €360bn+ trade gap
events.why_it_matters: Šefčovič wants 'initial/tangible' Chinese commitments on export surges, EU market access, and critical materials before an October Beijing trip and the mid-October EU leaders' summit — a fuse under EVs, chemicals, machinery, and e-commerce platforms.
events.what_to_watch: The ~Sept 17 trade-chiefs videoconference and whether Brussels tees up extra FSR/procurement tools if pilots disappoint.

events.title: Fed Beige Book — modest activity, moderate price gains into FOMC
events.why_it_matters: Anecdotes collected through Aug 24 showed slight-to-moderate growth in 10 of 12 districts, very slight job gains, and still-moderate selling-price increases with energy/tariff cost pressure — a hawkish-leaning color card for Warsh's first SEP.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Sept 16 press conference cites Beige Book margin squeeze vs. still-firm prices as the reason to hike.

events.title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (September)
events.why_it_matters: Builder sentiment prints the same morning as retail sales and the FOMC; August HMI was only 35, with 63% of builders still using incentives — a high-frequency read on rate-shock housing before Lennar.
events.what_to_watch: A drop back through 34 plus another rise in price-cutting would confirm the starts/permits miss risk on Sept 17.

events.title: US initial jobless claims (week ending Sept 12)
events.why_it_matters: The first labor print after the FOMC; consensus 205–208k after 206k prior, so a break higher would challenge the 'labor still tight enough to hike' narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Four-week average vs ~206k and continuing claims near 1.77–1.79m.

events.title: UK August retail sales (ONS)
events.why_it_matters: Lands the morning after the BoE hold decision; BRC already showed August sales slowing to +0.7% y/y and CBI distributive trades at −48, so a weak official print would validate a longer pause at 3.75%.
events.what_to_watch: Volume ex-auto fuel vs food/non-food split; GBP and UK retail names if the ONS confirms the BRC/CBI downshift.

events.title: Darden Restaurants Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Casual-dining same-store sales are a high-beta read on the US consumer the same day as the Trump-Xi summit, with food inflation and 5%+ mortgage rates already squeezing traffic.
events.what_to_watch: Olive Garden/LongHorn comps, commodity inflation (especially proteins after the livestock EOs), and FY27 traffic guidance.

events.title: Bessent: US yen-intervention role was 'nominal'; USD/JPY ~154–155
events.why_it_matters: Confirms July–August coordinated yen-buying (~¥15.4tn Japan, modest US) while USD/JPY sits in the 152–155 exporter-pain zone heading into a widely expected BoJ hike to 1.25%.
events.what_to_watch: Whether MOF re-enters if the BoJ under-delivers and USD/JPY rips back through 155–158; Japanese exporter FX guidance.

events.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September)
events.why_it_matters: August CCI already slipped to 89.4 with expectations in contraction; the late-month print is the last consumer-sentiment check before JOLTS and into the Trump-Xi hangover.
events.what_to_watch: Expectations index vs present situation, and inflation/jobs differentials after UMich's 4.6% 1-year inflation jump.

events.title: FOMC decision, SEP/dot plot, Warsh press conference
events.why_it_matters: Markets price ~87-92% odds of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% — the first hike under Chair Warsh — so the SEP/dots and presser matter more than the move itself.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the median 2026 dots imply another hike and whether Warsh refuses to pre-commit, which would keep the 10-year bidless.

events.title: August advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is +0.8% MoM after July's -0.6% collapse; a second miss 5.5 hours before the Fed would sharpen the hike-into-weakness/stagflation narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales vs ~+0.4% consensus; a miss plus a hawkish FOMC is the worst mix for discretionary retail.

events.title: 10-year Treasury yield holds at/above 5%
events.why_it_matters: The 10-year tagged ~5.01-5.03% and was still ~5.00% on Sept 15 — a multi-year high that is a direct valuation headwind for duration, housing, and utilities into the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a hawkish Warsh presser pushes a clean break above 5.10% or a hold/dovish surprise snaps yields back.

events.title: August CPI — headline 3.4% locks in September hike
events.why_it_matters: Headline CPI printed 3.4% y/y / 0.4% m/m with energy +16.3% y/y; core eased to 2.4% y/y but the oil shock and Warsh's Jackson Hole line drove hike odds from the 60s to ~90%.
events.what_to_watch: How much of the energy impulse Warsh treats as persistent vs transitory in the SEP inflation path.

events.title: Bank of Japan decision — hike to 1.25% widely expected
events.why_it_matters: OIS/polls assign ~97% odds to a 25bp hike to 1.25% (fastest pace of this cycle); landing 48 hours after a hawkish Fed is the classic yen-carry unwind setup.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's terminal-rate language and any hint of a larger-than-25bp move; a hawkish surprise would hit global risk via JPY funding.

events.title: Bank of England decision — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: Economists expect a hold after the 6-3 July vote, but oil >$100 has lifted hike odds to ~30-42% and three MPC members already wanted a hike.
events.what_to_watch: Dissent count, QT slowdown, and whether Bailey flags November as live if energy inflation sticks.

events.title: ECB 25bp hike; hawkish forecast upgrade; new rates effective
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate is 2.50% (effective Sept 16) after a second 2026 hike, with staff explicitly citing Iran-war energy inflation and lifting growth forecasts.
events.what_to_watch: Whether euro-area front-end follows Warsh higher this week or prices the ECB as done.

events.title: China August activity — IP beats, retail and FAI miss
events.why_it_matters: IP rose 5.2% y/y (beat) but retail sales slowed to 0.4% and Jan-Aug FAI fell 7.2%, confirming export/tech strength vs a domestic demand slump ahead of the Xi visit.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Beijing answers with fiscal/credit easing before Sept 24, or holds fire to keep leverage for the summit.

events.title: China August credit — new yuan loans collapse to 60bn
events.why_it_matters: New yuan loans were only ~60bn yuan vs ~400bn expected and outstanding loan growth hit a record-low 4.9% y/y, showing private credit demand is still broken.
events.what_to_watch: Sept 20-21 LPR fix and any RRR/structural-easing signal if loan demand stays dead.

events.title: PBOC September LPR fixing (hold expected)
events.why_it_matters: 1y LPR has been stuck at 3.0% and 5y at 3.5% for 15+ months; a hold after the credit collapse would confirm Beijing is using FX/liquidity tools, not benchmark cuts, into the summit.
events.what_to_watch: A surprise 5y cut would be bullish for China property/banks; a hold plus a strong yuan fix is the base case.

events.title: PBOC strengthens yuan fix into Trump-Xi
events.why_it_matters: The USD/CNY midpoint was set at 6.7670 on Sept 15, the fifth straight stronger fix, a political FX signal ahead of the Washington summit rather than a growth stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the fix stays firm through Sept 24 or snaps weaker if the Fed hikes and the dollar rips.

events.title: Bank of Korea minutes show 6-1 hike rift
events.why_it_matters: Minutes of the Aug 27 hike to 3.00% showed a 6-1 split, with the dissenter citing delinquencies even as chip-export boom and 3.1% CPI keep tightening live.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Seoul pauses while the Fed/BoJ hike, which would widen KRW/rate differentials and hit Korean financials.

events.title: US existing home sales fall to ~3.98m SAAR
events.why_it_matters: Sales dropped 2% m/m to 3.98 million as mortgage rates climbed with the 10-year, confirming housing is frozen heading into another Fed hike.
events.what_to_watch: Aug housing starts/permits on Sept 17 and Lennar's print on Sept 16 for confirmation the freeze is deepening.

events.title: August industrial production
events.why_it_matters: The first hard-activity print after the oil spike and into the Fed/BoJ week; a miss would reinforce stagflation, a beat would validate Warsh hiking.
events.what_to_watch: Manufacturing vs utilities/mining split — energy-related mining strength can mask factory weakness.

events.title: US-Iran tanker war; Brent ~$105-108, Hormuz impaired
events.why_it_matters: Six months into the war, Hormuz transits are down to single digits, the Saudi East-West pipeline remains disrupted, and Brent is holding $104-108 — a live stagflation shock into every G4 central bank.
events.what_to_watch: Daily Hormuz vessel counts, any restart of Iran-Gulf talks, and whether Brent holds $100 through the FOMC.

events.title: Trump-Xi Washington summit
events.why_it_matters: Xi's state visit is the quarter's highest-stakes trade event — tariffs, AI, Taiwan, rare earths, Boeing/autos, and the Iran war — less than six weeks before US midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Whether they extend the Nov 10 truce and cut ~$30bn/side of 'non-sensitive' tariffs, or Taiwan arms-sales friction shrinks the communiqué to symbolism.

events.title: US-China trade truce expires Nov 10 — pre-summit positioning
events.why_it_matters: Section 301 exclusions and the 2025 tariff suspension lapse Nov 10; Sept 24 is the last realistic window to extend, so headlines will whip tariff-sensitive names.
events.what_to_watch: Leaks on agriculture/energy tariff cuts and whether Bessent stays 'not in a hurry' after the summit.

events.title: UNGA high-level week (Iran, energy, midterms backdrop)
events.why_it_matters: General debate runs Sept 22-26/28 with Iran's nuclear file at the UNSC and Tehran rejecting talks after Trump's 9/11-linked remarks; Xi is skipping UNGA for Washington.
events.what_to_watch: Any US/Iran/Gulf side-meetings on Hormuz access and whether Trump uses the podium to harden war aims before meeting Xi.

events.title: US-Canada Section 338 tariff changes and import bans
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations retarget 50% additional duties on Canadian autos/alcohol/dairy (effective Sept 15) and set import bans for Sept 29, stacking on Section 232.
events.what_to_watch: Canadian retaliation lists and whether auto/dairy supply chains get licensed exclusions before Sept 29.

events.title: Continuing resolution funds government through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: House passed the CR 370-48 on Sept 1 and Trump signed it, killing Sept 30 shutdown risk and pushing FY2027 fights into the lame duck; debt ceiling is a 2027 problem.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing near-term on funding; drop unless lame-duck spending/debt talk reappears post-midterms.

events.title: Oracle Q1 FY27 beat on AI cloud demand
events.why_it_matters: Revenue ~$19.3bn (+30% y/y) and cloud infra +121% with RPO $664bn; the print re-anchored the AI-capex complex just as rates hit 5%.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the FOMC multiple-compression overrides the backlog story in semis, power, and datacenter names.

events.title: Adobe Q3 FY26 beat; shares slipped on outlook
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $6.76bn and 1bn MAUs with a raised FY guide, but the stock sold off — a template for 'beat-and-drop' software into a hawkish Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Whether software duration keeps de-rating if Warsh's dots stay hawkish.

events.title: FedEx Q1 FY27 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Calendars cluster FDX around Sept 16 after the close (some list Sept 17/25); it is the cleanest global-trade/volume read into Hormuz disruption and a hawkish Fed.
events.what_to_watch: Express volumes, fuel surcharge commentary, and China/US trade-lane color ahead of Trump-Xi.

events.title: Costco Q4/FY26 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Consensus EPS ~$6.55-6.67 the same day as Trump-Xi; membership/traffic vs gasoline inflation is the best high-frequency read on the US consumer after retail sales.
events.what_to_watch: Traffic, mix, and any tariff/food-cost commentary tied to Canada and China.

events.title: Holtec Nuclear IPO (~$0.8-1.0bn)
events.why_it_matters: One of the larger US IPOs this window (~50m shares, $15-18) into an AI-power/nuclear bid and a 5% 10-year — a live test of whether energy-transition issuance still clears.
events.what_to_watch: Final pricing vs range and first-day aftermarket; a stumble would freeze other energy IPOs.

events.title: NSE of India IPO (~$2.7bn)
events.why_it_matters: ₹22,562cr National Stock Exchange deal is the period's largest listing and a gauge of EM risk appetite into a global rates shock.
events.what_to_watch: Anchor/subscription cover and listing premium; a flop would be a broader EM-issuance signal.

events.title: SpaceX staggered lockup tranche (~7%)
events.why_it_matters: Day-105 unlock (~328m shares / ~7%) hits the same day as Trump-Xi and Costco; not a full cliff, but a known supply event in a crowded AI/space complex.
events.what_to_watch: SPCX volume/price around Sept 24 and whether later Oct 9/24 tranches get pulled forward in sentiment.

events.title: Micron Taiwan union strike preparations
events.why_it_matters: The union is keeping strike preparations live over profit-sharing just as AI memory prices and Korea/Taiwan export boom are a core growth pillar.
events.what_to_watch: Whether talks fail into a walkout that hits DRAM/HBM supply into Q4.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure into Trump-Xi
events.why_it_matters: PLA/coast-guard presence east of Taiwan is expected to persist through the Sept 24 summit; Taiwan arms-sales friction was already cited as a visit-cancellation threat.
events.what_to_watch: Any large-scale exercise, cyber incident, or unsigned US arms package leaking during UNGA/summit week.

events.title: FERC approves CIP-014-4 physical-security standard and related CIP grid orders
events.why_it_matters: FERC's September open meeting locked in tighter physical-security and cybersecurity reliability rules for critical substations and bulk-power cyber systems, a capex/compliance shock for transmission owners already facing the bulk-power equipment emergency.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation timelines, utility capex guidance, and whether physical-attack assessments pull forward grid-hardening spend into 2027 rate cases.

events.title: FCC September open meeting: unlock ~1,000 MHz satellite spectrum and modernize NEPA rules
events.why_it_matters: The Sept 30 agenda would free ~550 MHz in 12.7–13.25 GHz and 500 MHz in 42–42.5 GHz for FSS/ESIM and declare many space-station and spectrum actions not 'major federal actions' under NEPA, cutting deployment friction for satellite broadband.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Report and Order is adopted as drafted, any earth-station/incumbent conditions, and the read-through to SpaceX, AST SpaceMobile, and satellite-broadband suppliers around the Sept 24 lockup.

events.title: House FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800, ~$1.15tn) received in the Senate
events.why_it_matters: The House-passed $1.15tn defense authorization arrived in the Senate after the Senate's own NDAA (S. 4784) stalled on a July cloture fail, reopening the must-pass defense-policy vehicle for procurement, shipbuilding, and industrial-base riders.
events.what_to_watch: Whether leadership files a motion to proceed on H.R. 8800 or S. 4784 before the Dec 11 CR, and which China/export-control/shipyard provisions survive conference.

events.title: FDA approves Telix Pixclara (floretyrosine F-18) for glioma PET imaging
events.why_it_matters: Pixclara is the first FDA-approved FET-PET agent to distinguish recurrent glioma from treatment effect, a discrete radiopharma catalyst outside the primary's upcoming Sept 16–30 PDUFA cluster.
events.what_to_watch: Launch timing, reimbursement, and whether Telix guides any 2026 Pixclara revenue after excluding it from prior FY guidance.

events.title: August ISM Manufacturing PMI 54.6; prices paid stuck at 71.1
events.why_it_matters: Factory activity stayed in expansion but cooled 1.0pt below ~55.2 consensus while prices paid held at 71.1, a hawkish input-cost signal into the Warsh FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: September ISM (Oct 1) and whether prices-paid stays extreme after the energy spike in PPI.

events.title: August ISM Services PMI 55.4; prices paid jump to 72.6
events.why_it_matters: Services expanded for a 26th month and beat consensus, but employment contracted (47.8) while prices paid rose 2.3pts to 72.6 — stagflationary mix that reinforces a September hike.
events.what_to_watch: FOMC statement language on services inflation and the next services PMI after the rate decision.

events.title: ADP August private payrolls +38k
events.why_it_matters: Private-sector hiring slowed to +38k versus NFP +162k, a labor-market divergence the primary's NFP item did not capture and a potential offset to hike-driven financials.
events.what_to_watch: September ADP (~Sept 30) and whether claims stay near 206k or start to confirm the ADP slowdown.

events.title: July factory orders +0.9% on civilian aircraft
events.why_it_matters: Headline orders beat as transportation jumped 2.3% and civilian aircraft/parts surged 12.7%, a narrow aerospace-bookings signal rather than broad factory strength.
events.what_to_watch: August durable goods on Sept 25 for whether the aircraft bounce repeats or core capex orders stall.

events.title: Palo Alto Networks Q4 FY2026 earnings beat; NGS ARR $9.1bn
events.why_it_matters: The cybersecurity bellwether printed $3.41bn revenue (+34%), NGS ARR $9.10bn (+63%), and record $21.2bn RPO, with FY27 revenue guided to $14.1–14.2bn — the main missed second-tier earnings print in the window.
events.what_to_watch: Whether peers (CRWD/FTNT) re-rate on platformization/AI-security demand and if FY27 margin guide holds after the Console deal.

events.title: August new-home sales (Census/HUD)
events.why_it_matters: July sales already slumped to 607k SAAR with 9.6 months' supply; the August print is the clean builder-demand read after existing-home sales hit a 2026 low and into Lennar's report.
events.what_to_watch: SAAR vs ~600–660k, months' supply, and incentive/price cuts as mortgage rates track the 5% 10-year.

events.title: August advance durable goods orders
events.why_it_matters: July durables already rose 1.1% on transportation; the August advance is the next capex/aircraft check after ISM new orders cooled to 53.7.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs core capital goods (nondefense ex-aircraft) and whether Boeing/defense bookings again dominate the print.

events.title: US 2-year note auction
events.why_it_matters: Primary covered the 10-year and 30-year reopenings but not the next short-end coupon; with hike odds elevated and 2s near 4.6–4.7%, a tail would extend the front-end selloff.
events.what_to_watch: High yield vs when-issued, bid-to-cover, and indirect takedown after the FOMC dots.

top_risks: Hawkish first Warsh FOMC (dots/presser) into a 5% 10-year — duration, housing, and high-multiple tech de-rate
Hormuz/Iran war keeps Brent >$100, forcing G4 central banks to hike into an energy shock (stagflation)
Fed + BoJ hiking 48 hours apart triggers a yen-carry unwind
Trump-Xi disappointment: no Nov 10 truce extension, Taiwan friction, or tariff re-escalation
China domestic demand/credit collapse with no benchmark easing into the summit
top_opportunities: Energy producers and oilfield/tanker names if Hormuz stays impaired and OPEC+ stays on hold
Truce-extension / agriculture-energy tariff-cut headlines around Sept 24
AI-cloud/semicap complex if Oracle-style backlog outruns the rates hit
China stimulus surprise if Beijing answers the 60bn-yuan loan print before Xi lands
BoE hold vs Fed/BoJ hike — relative UK duration/sterling if Bailey stays patient
summary: The next 48 hours are a stacked global-tightening event: US retail sales then Warsh's first FOMC hike (highly priced), followed by BoE (hold expected) and a near-certain BoJ hike to 1.25%. Overlay is a still-hot Iran/Hormuz oil shock with Brent ~$105-108 and a 5% 10-year, then a Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit that is the last clean window to extend the Nov 10 tariff truce. China just confirmed the split (strong IP, dead credit/retail), so the market is pricing policy, war, and geopolitics — not a quiet data week.

catcher.coverage_assessment: Primary was strong on the FOMC/CPI/PCE stack, Iran-oil, US-China truce/summit, CR, EPA power-plant repeal, OFAC, Canada 338, Google remedies, and the listed housing/Fed-survey prints. It was blind on agency open meetings (FERC CIP, FCC satellite/NEPA), the NDAA's Senate arrival, ISM/ADP/factory-orders, cybersecurity earnings (PANW), and the new-home-sales/durables/2-year calendar. It logged the CLARITY procedural vote but not the cloture failure; that is an update to a covered event, not a new miss.
catcher.biggest_gap: FCC Sept 30 open meeting unlocking ~1,000 MHz of satellite spectrum and streamlining NEPA for space/spectrum deployments — a dated agency catalyst sitting next to the SpaceX lockup that the primary did not list.
